subject: physics
title: Domestic uses and safety
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Domestic uses and safety — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.2.3.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Domestic uses and safety, specification section 4.2.3.
final_note: You worked through Domestic uses and safety — 12 specification statements.

concepts.def: A supply in which the potential difference repeatedly changes direction, so the current it drives repeatedly reverses direction. Mains electricity is an ac supply.
A potential difference that is always in the same direction, so the current it drives passes round the circuit in one direction only. Cells and batteries supply a direct potential difference.

The frequency of an ac supply is the number of complete cycles of the alternating potential difference each second, measured in hertz (Hz). In the United Kingdom the domestic supply has a frequency of 50 Hz.

concepts.term: Mains potential difference in the UK
concepts.def: The United Kingdom domestic electricity supply is about 230 V. This is the potential difference the live wire carries relative to earth.
The cable used to connect most electrical appliances to the mains. It contains three separately insulated wires: the live wire, the neutral wire and the earth wire.
The wire with brown insulation. It carries the alternating potential difference from the supply, and is at about 230 V relative to earth.
The wire with blue insulation. It completes the circuit, and is at, or close to, earth potential (0 V).
The wire with green and yellow striped insulation. It is a safety wire to stop the appliance becoming live. It is at 0 V and only carries a current if there is a fault.
The insulation covering each wire in a mains cable is colour coded for easy identification: live wire brown, neutral wire blue, earth wire green and yellow stripes.
The potential of the ground, taken as 0 V. Potential differences in a mains circuit are measured relative to this zero.

concepts.term: Potential difference between live and earth
concepts.def: The potential difference between the live wire and earth (0 V) is about 230 V. This is what drives a current through anything that connects the live wire to earth.

The neutral wire is at, or close to, earth potential (0 V). This is why the potential difference across an appliance is about 230 V even though only one of its two supply wires is at a high potential.

A fault in which the live wire comes into contact with a conducting part of an appliance, such as a metal case, so that part is raised to about 230 V. The earth wire is the safety wire that stops this happening.

concepts.term: Danger from a live wire with the switch open
concepts.def: Opening a switch in the mains circuit breaks the circuit, but the live wire on the supply side of the switch is still connected to the supply and is still at about 230 V relative to earth. Touching it is therefore still dangerous.

Any connection between the live wire and earth places about 230 V across that path. If the path is a person, or a low-resistance conductor, a large current passes through it, which is why such connections are dangerous.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes the domestic electricity supply in the United Kingdom?
options: An alternating supply of about 230 V with a frequency of 50 Hz
A direct supply of about 230 V with a frequency of 50 Hz
An alternating supply of about 50 V with a frequency of 230 Hz
A direct supply of about 230 V with no frequency at all
mcqs.explain: Mains electricity is an ac supply; in the UK the domestic supply has a frequency of 50 Hz and is about 230 V.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a direct and an alternating potential difference?
options: A direct potential difference is always in the same direction; an alternating one repeatedly reverses
A direct potential difference never changes in size; an alternating one changes in size only
A direct potential difference moves charge round a circuit; an alternating one moves none
A direct potential difference comes from the mains; an alternating one comes from a cell
mcqs.explain: Direction is the defining difference: a direct potential difference acts one way only, an alternating one keeps changing direction.

mcqs.q: The UK domestic supply has a frequency of 50 Hz. What does this tell you about the supply?
options: The alternating potential difference completes 50 full cycles each second
The potential difference at the socket is 50 volts rather than 230 volts
The potential difference changes size 50 times a second, in one direction
The supply transfers 50 joules of energy to an appliance every second
mcqs.explain: Frequency in hertz is the number of complete cycles per second, so 50 Hz means 50 complete cycles of the alternating potential difference every second.

mcqs.q: The outer covering of a three-core cable is cut back. Which set of colours identifies the three wires correctly?
options: Live blue, neutral brown, earth green and yellow stripes
Live brown, neutral green and yellow stripes, earth blue
Live green and yellow stripes, neutral blue, earth brown
Live brown, neutral blue, earth green and yellow stripes
mcqs.explain: This is the colour coding given in the specification: live wire brown, neutral wire blue, earth wire green and yellow stripes.

mcqs.q: What is the job of the earth wire in a three-core cable?
options: It carries unwanted current away from the appliance all the time
It is a safety wire that stops the appliance becoming live
It completes the circuit so that charge can pass round it
It supplies the alternating potential difference to the appliance
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the earth wire is a safety wire to stop the appliance becoming live.

mcqs.q: In a mains circuit, what is the job of the neutral wire?
options: It completes the circuit, and is at or close to 0 V
It is the safety wire that stops the case becoming live
It carries the alternating potential difference from the supply
It only carries a current when there is a fault somewhere
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the neutral wire completes the circuit and is at, or close to, earth potential (0 V).

mcqs.q: A voltmeter is connected between the neutral wire and earth in a mains circuit that is working normally. What reading is expected?
options: About 230 V, because the neutral wire is part of the same circuit
About 230 V, because the neutral wire carries the supply to earth
About 0 V, because the neutral wire is at or close to earth potential
About 115 V, because the 230 V is shared between the two wires
mcqs.explain: The neutral wire is at, or close to, earth potential (0 V), so there is almost no potential difference between it and earth.

mcqs.q: When does the earth wire of an appliance carry a current?
options: All the time the appliance is switched on
Whenever the neutral wire carries a current
Only while a switch in the plug is open
Only when there is a fault in the appliance
mcqs.explain: The earth wire is at 0 V and only carries a current if there is a fault.

mcqs.q: A lamp is plugged into a wall socket but its own switch is open. Which statement about the live wire inside the lamp is correct?
options: It is at 0 V, because the open switch disconnects it from the supply
It is still at about 230 V relative to earth, so it is still dangerous
It is safe to touch, as long as the neutral wire is not touched too
It is at 0 V, and the neutral wire is now at about 230 V instead
mcqs.explain: An open switch stops a current but does not disconnect the live wire from the supply, so it remains at about 230 V relative to earth.

mcqs.q: A person standing on damp ground touches a bare live wire. Why is this dangerous?
options: It is only dangerous if the neutral wire is touched at the same time
It is only dangerous if the appliance is switched on at the wall
It connects live to earth, so about 230 V drives a current through them
The earth wire will carry the current, so the danger is a fire risk
mcqs.explain: Any connection between the live wire and earth has about 230 V across it, and here the person is that connection.

mcqs.q: Inside a metal-cased heater the live wire works loose and touches the metal case. The case is connected to the earth wire. What happens?
options: Nothing changes, because the earth wire already carries a current anyway
The neutral wire carries the fault current, since it is also at 0 V
The case stays at about 230 V until somebody touches it and is shocked
A large current passes in the earth wire, as live is now joined to earth
mcqs.explain: The fault provides a connection between the live wire and earth, and about 230 V across that low-resistance path drives a large current.

mcqs.q: Most electrical appliances are connected to the mains using three-core cable. What does three-core cable contain?
options: Three wires that all carry a current when the appliance works
Three separately insulated wires: live, neutral and earth
Three layers of insulation, to make the appliance safer to use
A live wire and two wires that both complete the circuit
mcqs.explain: Three-core cable contains the live, neutral and earth wires, each with its own colour-coded insulation.

mcqs.q: Why is the insulation covering each wire inside a mains cable colour coded?
options: So that each wire is allowed to carry a different size of current
So that the earth wire can be seen while it is carrying a current
So that the live wire's insulation can withstand a higher voltage
So that each wire can be quickly identified when a plug is wired
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the insulation covering each wire is colour coded for easy identification.

mcqs.q: A plug is wired incorrectly, and the brown wire is connected to the earth pin. What is the immediate danger?
options: There is no danger, because the brown wire is the neutral wire anyway
There is no danger, because the earth wire is always held at 0 V
The earth pin, and any metal case joined to it, is now at about 230 V
The appliance will not work, but there is no electrical danger at all
mcqs.explain: Brown is the live wire, so connecting it to the earth pin puts the earth wire and anything joined to it at about 230 V.

mcqs.q: A student says that a cell and a mains socket both supply an alternating potential difference. What is wrong with this?
options: Nothing is wrong: both reverse, which is why no charge moves at all
A cell supplies a direct potential difference, in one direction only
Nothing is wrong: both change in size, and that is what alternating means
The mains supplies a direct potential difference and a cell alternates
mcqs.explain: Only the mains supply is ac; a cell supplies a direct potential difference, which does not change direction.

mcqs.q: In a mains circuit that is working normally, how does the potential of the neutral wire compare with earth?
options: It is at about 230 V, the same as the live wire is
It is at exactly 0 V at all times, with no exception
It is at, or close to, earth potential, which is 0 V
It is at about 115 V, halfway between live and earth
mcqs.explain: The specification states the neutral wire is at, or close to, earth potential (0 V).
